items.q: Echo shows thickened mitral leaflets with diastolic doming and commissural fusion. What is the diagnosis?
items.exp: Doming with fused commissures marks rheumatic mitral obstruction, unlike calcified aortic disease or cavity dilatation. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2017 stenosis guideline, section on mitral stenosis morphology.

items.q: Mitral valve area is 0.8 sq cm with mean gradient 12 mmHg. What grade is this?
items.exp: Area below 1.0 with gradient above 10 meets the severe bands with left atrial pressure load. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2017 stenosis guideline, section on mitral stenosis severity.

items.q: Echo shows calcified aortic cusps with restricted opening and a high velocity jet. What is the diagnosis?
items.exp: Thick still cusps with a fast systolic jet and small orifice define aortic stenosis rather than leak or shunt. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2017 stenosis guideline, section on aortic stenosis morphology.

items.q: Peak velocity is 4.5 m per s with mean gradient 48 mmHg and area 0.8 sq cm. What grade is this?
items.exp: Velocity above 4 with gradient above 40 and area below 1.0 meets all three severe bands. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2017 stenosis guideline, section on aortic stenosis severity.

items.q: A posteriorly directed mitral jet with leaflet prolapse and a dilated left atrium fits what?
items.exp: Prolapse with an eccentric jet plus chronic chamber enlargement marks longstanding severe mitral leak. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on mitral regurgitation signs.

items.q: EROA is 0.45 sq cm with regurgitant volume 65 ml in mitral regurgitation. What grade is this?
items.exp: Orifice at or above 0.40 with volume at or above 60 meets the severe bands. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on mitral regurgitation severity.

items.q: A diastolic jet in the outflow with vena contracta 7 mm fits what?
items.exp: A wide diastolic neck above 6 mm shows a large leak orifice rather than obstruction. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on aortic regurgitation signs.

items.q: Aortic regurgitation shows pressure half time 180 ms with holodiastolic reversal. What grade fits?
items.exp: Short half time with runoff through all of diastole marks a large leak with fast pressure equalisation. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on aortic regurgitation severity.

items.q: Dilated right atrium and ventricle with a wide tricuspid jet fit what?
items.exp: Right chamber enlargement with a large coaptation gap marks tricuspid leak rather than left sided disease. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on tricuspid regurgitation signs.

items.q: Tricuspid EROA is 0.50 sq cm with vena contracta 8 mm. What grade is this?
items.exp: Orifice at or above 0.40 with neck at or above 7 mm meets the severe bands. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on tricuspid regurgitation severity.

items.q: Asymmetric septal thickening with a small cavity and a harsh murmur fits what?
items.exp: Disproportionate septal hypertrophy with a tiny cavity defines HCM rather than dilated or fluid disease. Guideline: ESC valvular heart disease guideline, section on hypertrophic cardiomyopathy.

items.q: Septal thickness is 18 mm with systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve. What fits?
items.exp: Marked thickness with SAM draws the leaflet into the outflow and creates a dynamic gradient. Guideline: ESC valvular heart disease guideline, section on obstructive HCM.

items.q: A dilated thin walled left ventricle with ejection fraction 28 percent fits what?
items.exp: A large cavity with poor squeeze and thin walls marks dilated systolic failure rather than thick or compressed hearts. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on chamber size and function.

items.q: Dilated cardiomyopathy with left bundle disease and severe symptoms may need what device thought?
o: Resynchronisation assessment per heart failure protocol
items.exp: Wide dyssynchronous failure may gain from resynchronisation, so protocol review follows echo. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on dilated cavity management.

items.q: Concentric wall thickening with a normal sized cavity and hypertension fits what?
o: Left ventricular hypertrophy from pressure load
items.exp: Even thick walls with preserved cavity mark pressure driven hypertrophy rather than dilated or obstructive disease. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on remodelling patterns.

items.q: Septal thickness of 14 mm with hypertension and no SAM is best labelled what?
o: Hypertensive hypertrophy with HCM kept in review
items.exp: Mid range thickness with pressure load favours hypertensive change, yet family and ECG review keep HCM open. Guideline: ESC valvular heart disease guideline, section on hypertrophy differential.

items.q: A black echo free space around the whole heart with preserved motion fits what?
items.exp: Fluid in the pericardial sac rims the heart through the cycle, unlike pleural fluid above the diaphragm. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on pericardium.

items.q: Effusion size is judged by what echo measure?
o: Maximal echo free separation through the cycle
items.exp: The widest blood to heart gap reflects volume, so separation rather than rate or thickness sizes it. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on pericardial effusion.

items.q: Right atrial collapse with diastolic right ventricular collapse and a plethoric cava fits what?
items.exp: Chamber collapse in diastole with a full cava shows pressure blocking filling, which defines tamponade. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on tamponade signs.

items.q: Respiratory variation with tamponade shows what pattern?
o: Exaggerated inflow change across the valves with breathing
items.exp: Ventricular interdependence rises under pressure, so inflow swings widely with each breath. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on tamponade signs.

items.q: Anterior wall akinesia after chest pain with a new wall motion defect fits what?
o: Infarct in the left anterior descending territory
items.exp: A fresh regional defect matching pain marks ischaemic stunning or scar in that coronary territory. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on wall motion assessment.

items.q: Which coronary territory supplies the anterior wall and anterior septum?
items.exp: The anterior descending vessel runs down the front groove feeding septum and front wall. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on coronary territories.

items.q: Dilated right chambers with a secundum defect at the fossa fits what?
items.exp: Left to right atrial shunting volume loads the right side, and the gap sits at the fossa ovalis. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on septal defects.

items.q: A high velocity jet across the interventricular septum in systole fits what?
items.exp: Systolic left to right flow through the septum with a fast jet marks a ventricular defect. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on septal defects.

items.q: A continuous colour jet between the aorta and pulmonary artery in a newborn fits what?
items.exp: The duct joins great vessels with flow through systole and diastole, so a continuous jet there is ductal. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on ductal imaging.

items.q: Overriding aorta with ventricular defect, outflow narrowing and right hypertrophy fits what?
items.exp: The four features travel together as one cyanotic lesion rather than separate defects. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on congenital lesions.

items.q: Flattened septum in systole with raised tricuspid velocity fits what?
items.exp: High right pressure pushes the septum flat while the fast jet quantifies the load. Guideline: ASE right heart quantification guideline, section on pulmonary hypertension.

items.q: An echogenic mass at the apex beside an aneurysm after infarction fits what?
items.exp: Stasis beside dead akinetic wall breeds mural clot, unlike infected valve tissue or stalked tumours. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on masses and thrombus.

items.q: An oscillating mass on a valve with new regurgitation and fever fits what?
items.exp: Mobile infected tissue on the leaflet with destructive leak and sepsis marks endocarditis. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on vegetations.

items.q: A mobile linear echo in the aortic lumen with flow on both sides fits what?
items.exp: An independent flap with true and false channels moves unlike fixed artefact or simple clot. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on aortic imaging.

items.q: Commissural fusion with doming and subvalvar thickening in a young adult in India most suggests what cause?
items.exp: Rheumatic disease is common in India and scars commissures with chordal thickening, unlike wear with age. Guideline: ASE and EACVI 2017 stenosis guideline, section on rheumatic morphology.

items.q: Why does rheumatic mitral disease matter more in Indian practice?
o: It is common and presents young with atrial fibrillation risk
items.exp: High prevalence with early severe disease and clot risk shapes screening and follow up across clinics. Guideline: ESC valvular heart disease guideline, section on rheumatic disease burden.

items.q: A young adult with a bicuspid aortic valve and ascending dilatation needs what follow up?
o: Serial root measurement with activity and family advice
items.exp: Bicuspid roots can dilate and dissect, so tracked measurement with family screening is the safe path. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on bicuspid valve and aorta.

items.q: In obstructive HCM the murmur grows louder with Valsalva and standing because of what?
o: Less preload shrinking the cavity and worsening obstruction
items.exp: Small volumes bring walls and SAM closer, so obstruction and murmur rise as load falls. Guideline: ESC valvular heart disease guideline, section on dynamic obstruction.

items.q: Tamponade with a large effusion differs from a large effusion without tamponade by what?
items.exp: Size alone does not compress, so diastolic collapse with a full cava proves physiology beyond volume. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on tamponade signs.

items.q: A stalked mobile mass attached to the septum in the left atrium fits what over thrombus?
items.exp: A narrow stalk with attachment to the fossa region marks tumour, while clot sits broad based in the appendage. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on masses and thrombus.

items.q: A dissection flap is suspected but seen in one frame only. What confirms it?
o: Persistence in two planes with colour in true and false lumens
items.exp: Artefact vanishes with plane change, while true flaps persist across cuts with flow on both sides. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on aortic imaging.

items.q: Squatting eases a cyanotic spell in tetralogy because of what?
o: Raised systemic resistance cutting right to left shunt
items.exp: Higher afterload holds blood in the lungs rather than across the defect, so saturation rises with posture. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on tetralogy physiology.

items.q: Pulmonary vein systolic reversal supports which severe left sided leak?
items.exp: Atrial pressure waves flood backward in systole only when the mitral leak is large. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on supporting signs.

items.q: Dilated left ventricle with EF 30 percent and Q waves anteriorly after infarction suggests what?
items.exp: Scar Q waves with a weak dilated pump mark burnt muscle rather than trained or compressed hearts. Guideline: ASE 2015 chamber quantification guideline, section on ischaemic remodelling.

items.q: Holodiastolic reversal in the descending aorta supports which severe leak?
items.exp: Runoff through all of diastole needs a large aortic hole rather than a small or no leak. Guideline: ASE 2017 valvular regurgitation guideline, section on descending aorta flow.

items.q: What echo sign shows a haemodynamically important atrial septal defect?
o: Dilated right chambers with volume overload
items.exp: A shunt large enough to matter swells the right side, so right dilatation proves significance. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on shunt assessment.

items.q: A small restrictive ventricular septal defect shows which jet?
o: Fast high velocity left to right jet
items.exp: A tiny hole holds a large pressure gap, so the jet screams across at high velocity. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on septal defects.

items.q: A large ductus in a preterm infant causes which echo picture?
o: Pulmonary overcirculation with left volume load
items.exp: Runoff into the lungs floods them while the left heart carries the extra return. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on ductal imaging.

items.q: Crying triggers a cyanotic spell in tetralogy. What eases it?
o: Knee chest posture with oxygen and calm
items.exp: Raising systemic resistance with calm and oxygen cuts the right to left shunt until care arrives. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on tetralogy physiology.

items.q: TR velocity is 3.4 m per s with right atrial pressure 10 mmHg. What is PASP?
items.exp: Bernoulli gives 4 times 11.56 near 46, and adding atrial pressure 10 gives about 56 systolic. Guideline: ASE right heart quantification guideline, section on pulmonary pressure estimation.

items.q: An apical mass with high embolism risk looks like what?
o: Mobile protruding thrombus into the cavity
items.exp: A moving tip in flow breaks off more readily than flat organised clot, so shape guides urgency. Guideline: ASE 2019 TTE guideline, section on masses and thrombus.

items.q: Small vegetations are missed on surface echo. What is the next test?
o: Transoesophageal echo for closer higher frequency views
items.exp: The probe behind the heart resolves millimetre lesions that surface views miss. Guideline: ASE and SCA TEE guideline 2013, section on indications.
